findings.location:
Daar is peace lilies, roses, hibiscus ...

(paragraph beginning "Maar ek het vreugde gevind in een klein plekkie grond...")
findings.source_quote: There are peace lilies, roses, hibiscus, and other bright flowers blooming, and succulents growing in delightful little pots.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the standard Afrikaans plural for "peace lily". Replace "vredelelieë" with "vredelelies" (or "vredeleliese" if you prefer a different plural form) so it reads naturally: "Daar is vredelelies, rose, hibiskus ..."
findings.translation_quote: Daar is vredelelieë, rose, hibiskus en ander helder blomme wat blom, en vetplante wat in lieflike potte groei.

findings.location: Gooi die slappe, lelike gordyn ... (paragraph in section "Om die huis redelik skoon en behaaglik te hou")
findings.source_quote: (yes, even if it does take a few dollars to do so, I remind my penny-pinching soul).
findings.suggested_fix: "stuursugtige siel" is understandable but uncommon in contemporary Afrikaans. Consider a more idiomatic rendering such as "my gierige siel" or "my krenterige siel" to better reflect "penny‑pinching soul": "(ja, selfs al kos dit ’n paar dollars om te doen, herinner ek my gierige siel daaraan)."
findings.translation_quote: (ja, selfs al kos dit ’n paar dollars om te doen, herinner ek my stuursugtige siel daaraan).
